title: Finiteness of E[e^{2M}] asserted but not justified for M = sup Z

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Lemma `lem:disc`, the Cauchy-Schwarz step $\mathbb E[e^M\omega_\delta]\le(\mathbb E[e^{2M}])^{1/2}(\mathbb E[\omega_\delta^2])^{1/2}$, where $M=\sup_{t\le T}Z(t)=\sup_{t\le T}(\eta(t)-\tfrac12\sigma^2(t))$.

**Gap.** The proof invokes "Borell-TIS (Gaussian suprema have finite exponential moments)" for $\mathbb E[\Omega^2]<\infty$ with $\Omega=2\sup|Z|$, but the step that actually needs justification is $\mathbb E[e^{2M}]<\infty$. Borell-TIS concerns $\sup\eta$, not directly $\sup(\eta-\tfrac12\sigma^2)$. The argument should be stated: since $M\le\sup_{t\le T}\eta(t)$, $\mathbb E[e^{2M}]\le\mathbb E[e^{2\sup_{t\le T}\eta(t)}]$, and by the Borell-TIS concentration inequality $\sup_{t\le T}\eta(t)$ has a sub-Gaussian upper tail, so $\mathbb E[e^{\lambda\sup\eta}]<\infty$ for every $\lambda$; in particular for $\lambda=2$. (The hypothesis $\sup_{t\le T}\mathrm{Var}\,\eta(t)<\infty$ needed for Borell-TIS holds since $\sigma^2$ is finite/continuous on $[0,T]$.)

**Severity.** Minor; one-line fix, but currently the dependence on the $-\tfrac12\sigma^2$ term and the precise theorem hypotheses are glossed over.
